stories.headline: Trump says further US attacks on Iran are unlikely after talks with Qatar

sources.body:
Donald Trump has said "Iran militarily is effectively over", and said that there is "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the Middle East conflict.

"We're just keeping it the status quo," the US president said on Monday. "And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours."

Addressing reporters from the White House press briefing room, Trump said that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" but that the US was "locked and loaded" should the circumstances change.

Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed doubts about Trump's prior comments about resolving the conflict.

This is not the first time that Trump has said the Iran war is "militarily" over, but the circumstances for him are different now.

The president has hinted at de-escalation in Iran after a bruising set of midterm election results for the Republicans last week, which senior figures including Vice-President JD Vance blamed on the Iran war.

Ahead of the midterms, Trump had said US forces conducted what he described as "minor strikes" on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz . However, in an interview with 60 Minutes that aired on Sunday, the president said that he did not currently see "any reason" to escalate the conflict.

Responding to a question over why he would not officially declare an end to the war, Trump said that some of the Gulf allies could still face Iranian aggression.

"We have some great allies there and we have to make sure they're not hurt," he said, suggesting that the US naval blockade on Iranian ports was helping to make the region more secure.

Trump hosted Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani in the Oval Office earlier on Monday, saying they had an "excellent conversation" about negotiations to end the war.

In a post on X, the Qatari leader said he held "positive discussions" with Trump and Vance on "reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region".

Efforts to broker a peace between Washington and Tehran have largely been held indirectly through mediators since the war first broke out following joint US-Israeli strikes in February.

Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are among the US's Gulf allies that have been hit by Iranian strikes over the course of the war, in addition to the threat of strikes that have led to major air travel disruptions in the region.

Post-election recriminations over the US war in Iran are already placing pressure on members of the Trump administration.

Republican congressman Thomas Massie launched a strong attack against Trump's Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over the war in Iran, requesting a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach him.

Trump has backed Hegseth, who says he is "not worried" about the looming impeachment threats, calling Massie's effort a "sham".

While the move is unlikely to succeed with Republicans still in control of Congress until January, Democrats have expressed willingness to impeach Hegseth once the new session begins and they have control of both the House and the Senate.
sources.headline: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'

sources.body:
Iranian officials dismissed Trump’s latest remarks as ‘fake news’ after the US president suggested keeping ‘status quo’.

United States President Donald Trump has signalled that he considers the US-Israel war on Iran “effectively” at an end, after meeting Qatar’s prime minister in Washington, DC.

In a surprise briefing on Monday, Trump reiterated his position that the US had destroyed Iran’s military. But his remarks suggested he faces pressure from allies in the Middle East to bring hostilities to a close.

“Iran militarily is effectively over,” he said. “We’re just keeping it the status quo, and we’re doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours.”

His comments followed a closed-door meeting with US Vice President JD Vance and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, who hailed the progress in a post on social media.

“We discussed the situation in the region and ways to progress the US-Iran talks,” the prime minister said. “Grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region.”

Still, Trump acknowledged the “status quo” would involve continuing the US naval blockade against Iranian ports, as well as the newly announced Task Force Iron Gate, which seeks to cut off trade by land and through the Caspian Sea.

“Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and others would prefer the status quo, that we remain as is,” he said. “In other words, a continuation of the greatest naval blockade in the history of our country. Probably in the history of the world.”

Trump also indicated in his briefing that the US was willing to resume fighting, should the need arise.

“Taking military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” he said.

“Israel and the entire Middle East are protected from Iranian danger and threats, and we’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.”

Iranian officials, meanwhile, dismissed Trump’s latest remarks as a distraction.

“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler,” Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei wrote in a post on social media.

“FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.”

Separately, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said that the country’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had called for an end to the situation, which he described as “neither war nor peace”.

Pezeshkian added that Iran was open to further negotiations but would not be coerced, according to Iranian media. “We will not surrender to force and bullying,” he said.

Since the war on Iran began on February 28, the conflict has spilled into surrounding countries and roiled international trade.

Almost as soon as the US and Israel began their attacks, Iran moved to shut down the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for oil, gas and fertiliser, among other goods.

Iran also responded to US and Israeli strikes with missile and drone fire on its neighbours in the Gulf, including Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and the UAE, with many of the attacks targeting US military installations.
sources.headline: After meeting Qatar PM, Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ militarily

stories.headline: Ukraine, Russia and US resume peace talks with security guarantees on the agenda

sources.body:
Zelenskyy claims Russia ‘suffering record losses’ as Trump says US seeing ‘strong inclination’ to end war in Ukraine.

Negotiators from Russia and Ukraine are set to meet for peace talks brokered by the United States in Abu Dhabi, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying that recent gains on the battlefield had strengthened his country’s hand.

The meeting in the capital of the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday will be the third round of talks there this year, following security consultations in January and February . The US side is led by US President Donald Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who have spearheaded Washington’s mediation.

The three delegations last met in Geneva on February 18.

“Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine’s negotiating position,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address on Monday. He said Russia was “suffering record losses”, a claim Moscow disputes, and urged Washington to persuade the Kremlin to end the war.

Zelenskyy said General Mykhailo Drapatyi had presented a report on Ukraine’s military positions that pointed to heavy recent Russian losses, and that Ukraine’s long-range strikes on targets inside Russia, including oil facilities, were having an effect.

“We are responding to Russia’s war in a fully justified manner and demonstrating that this war must end,” he said. “Russia can do this. It can end its war. It is important that the United States convince Russia of precisely this.”

In Washington, DC, Trump told reporters that he saw a “very strong inclination” towards ending the war and that both sides were “tired of fighting”.

“We’re having a very good conversation about that in Abu Dhabi,” he said.

Trump had promised to end the war quickly when he took office in January 2025, but a settlement has remained elusive nearly five years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

A US official, briefing reporters on the condition of anonymity, said on Monday that both Russia and Ukraine had privately shown some flexibility on a possible exchange of territory. Security guarantees for Ukraine would be a central topic, the official said, including the possibility of a defence commitment modelled on Article 5 of NATO’s founding treaty.

Both Ukraine and Russia have been adamant about territory .

Ukraine wants Russia pushed back to the original border between the two countries, while Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to obtain all of the Donbas region.

Russia occupies roughly 20 percent of Ukraine , including Crimea and parts of the eastern Donbas region. The Russian move has not been recognised by the international community, but Trump has previously urged Kyiv to cede territory for a deal to end the war.

The US official said any territorial agreement would most likely come at the end of the negotiations, once other issues, including a post-war security framework, had been settled.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio meanwhile struck a cautious note, saying that the process to end the war still has “a ways to go”.
sources.headline: Russia, Ukraine and US to meet as Zelenskyy claims battlefield successes

sources.body: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are set to meet in the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Tuesday for a new round of talks aimed at ending nearly five years of full-scale war triggered by Moscow's invasion of its neighbour. Security guarantees for the warring sides are set to top the agenda, with US officials insisting that a broader security architecture for Europe must be part of any peace deal.
sources.headline: What to expect as Russia, Ukraine and the US hold trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi

sources.body:
Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would controls Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, US officials have said.

The comments came on the eve of the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine since February.

Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington will meet in Abu Dhabi as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches.

Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.

"An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X.

But Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict in the first place remain far apart.

A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia.

Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security.

While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately".

However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture".

"They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other."

For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans.

The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022.

The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since.

Since then, European leaders - who have been largely excluded from peace talks – have pushed to be involved in the process amid concerns that decisions about the security of their continent would be made without them.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged on Monday to include Nato allies and EU members into any "meaningful discussions about Europe's security architecture". President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly stated Kyiv wanted Europe to be part of the talks.
sources.headline: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say

stories.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for supermarket refrigeration cyberattacks

sources.body:
French foreign minister vows European sanctions against Tehran over ‘unprecedented’ hacks last month

France has said Iran was responsible for a massive cyber-attack on supermarket freezers and chiller cabinets that was described by its foreign minister as being an act of “unprecedented scale and unprecedented aggression”.

Jean-Noël Barrot said “Europe-wide sanctions” would be imposed against those responsible, adding that the attacks – which took control of digital thermostats to push temperatures up to above 50C – constituted “a major violation of the nation’s interests”.

At a press briefing during the G7 summit in Paris, he said: “Thanks to the remarkable efforts of government agencies, I am able to confirm that the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Revolutionary Guards are responsible for this attack.”

He said the Iranian ambassador had been summoned “to protest in the strongest possible terms against this extremely serious act.”

Swathes of French supermarkets were hit in the cyber-attacks on 11 and 12 October. Some were forced to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

Similar incidents have been reported since, including on supermarket fridges in other European countries last week and on a French blood bank.

The Paris public prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said on Monday that specialist investigators and government agencies had identified “a modus operandi” characteristic of the Iranian group Shahid Kaveh, a cyber warfare unit linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC).

This included “the use of Farsi and IP addresses traced back to devices located in Iran”, she said.

Beccuau said her office had opened a investigation against the head of Shahid Kaveh, his deputies and “others who will be identified” on charges of “fraudulent attacks on an automated data processing system committed as part of an organised crime ring and of causing damage dangerous to persons”.

She said the offences were “aggravated by the fact they were committed to serve a foreign power – in this case Iran”.

Gérôme Billois, a partner at the cybersecurity and technology company Wavestone, said Shahid Kaveh had been active since 2020 and was known to have carried out cyber-attacks mostly on water distribution systems in the US.

“Two countries are known for this kind of attack: Iran and Russia. Given that recent cyber-attacks on supermarkets and the blood bank in France concerned freezers it is reasonable to think Iran is directly linked to both,” he said,

“For the moment they are attacking easy equipment but as a state group that has the means, the determination and the time, we should be prepared to see attacks on other systems like water or electricity.”

During the attack last month, hackers remotely overrode the temperature setting on thousands of freezers , fridges and chiller cabinets in as many as 700 supermarkets and shops across France, pushing them from as low as -27C (-16.6F) to well over 50C (122F) in some cases.

sources.body: France on Monday said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind "unprecedented" cyberattacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month, vowing sanctions on a European level against Tehran. Swathes of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators, in some cases forcing them to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.
sources.headline: France opens probe into Iranian cyber unit over fridge attacks

sources.body:
Paris says a cyber unit linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard was behind hack, which hit more than 1,000 stores.

France has opened an investigation and accused Iran of being behind recent cyberattacks targeting refrigeration units in supermarkets.

French authorities said on Monday that they are probing a cyber unit affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) over the attacks, which caused fires and large amounts of food waste.

Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said that the Iranian ambassador had been summoned and that sanctions would be sought against those responsible at a “European level”.

“I can confirm that this attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Barrot said of the cyberattacks on French supermarkets that occurred on October 11 and 12.

The Paris prosecutor’s office said it has requested international arrest warrants against the leader of Shahid Kaveh, an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the IRGC, and his two deputies.

Barrot told reporters that the attack was “unprecedented in its level of aggression”.

“This is the first large-scale cyberattack carried out for sabotage purposes on French soil,” he said. “It represents a major attack on the nation’s interests and on the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.”

“We will also take any other measures that are proportionate and necessary, whether public or private, to respond to this attack and deter anyone who might seek to repeat it,” Barrot added.

Investigators say the attackers used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices in Iran to carry out the attack, during which they gained internet access to the refrigeration systems and remotely cranked up temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight.

Millions of euros’ worth of food was spoiled, according to retailers. In some cases, the raised temperatures sparked fires or melted equipment.

French supermarket groups E-Leclerc, Intermarche, Carrefour, Monoprix and Cooperative U were all hit.

At least 300 of Intermarche’s stores and its Netto brand were affected. Cooperative U said more than 100 of its supermarkets were targeted, while Carrefour said 80 supermarkets were affected, and Monoprix reported that about 5 percent of its roughly 490 stores were hit.

Supermarkets in several other European countries reported similar refrigeration problems on November 2. Overnight temperature spikes were recorded in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden. Dozens of stores and a food distribution hub were hit.

Jody Westby, chief executive of Global Cyber Risk LLC, said tracking down the group directly responsible for the attacks is “very difficult” because of poor cooperation on international cybercrime investigations.

“It’s been a problem for 20 some years, and now it’s a little better, but only marginally so,” Westby told Al Jazeera, adding that it was difficult to track and trace the origin of such attacks “because of the nature of packet switching”.
sources.headline: France accuses Iran of cyberattack on supermarket fridges

stories.headline: More than 50,000 displaced by deadly border clashes in Ethiopia

sources.body:
Families arrive in Kenya with little food or shelter as host communities struggle to cope.

Moyale, Kenya – When Hawa Hassan fled her home in Ethiopia’s Moyale area, she left almost everything behind. Her house was burned during the violence, she said. But one memory has stayed with her: a 13-year-old girl shot while sitting near a wall.

Hassan said the girl had not touched a flag, a detail she raised while describing tensions over flag displays in the disputed border area. Her account of the killing could not be independently verified.

The journey into Kenya was brutal. Hassan told Al Jazeera that some women gave birth while fleeing, and that families arrived without food, cooking utensils or bedding. Newborn babies were sleeping on bare floors. Diarrhoea was spreading, while families feared malaria as mosquitoes multiplied.

For many, crossing the border has meant escaping gunfire only to face another struggle: finding food and shelter. The arrivals are also stretching Kenyan communities. Families that opened their homes are sharing scarce supplies, even as some worry the violence could reach their own neighbourhoods.

A government-led assessment conducted on October 29 and 30 estimated that 35,950 people had been displaced as of October 24. About 25,000 were staying with host families and nearly 11,000 in temporary displacement sites.

The number has since risen. During a meeting, Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan said the number of people displaced by the conflict had increased from an estimated 36,000 to more than 50,000. The figure includes people living in temporary settlements as well as those staying with relatives and host families.

The overall number of displaced people has yet to be independently established, and no final figure has been confirmed.

The assessment covered 758 households and involved government authorities, United Nations agencies, the Kenya Red Cross and other humanitarian organisations. The figures reflect different reporting periods.

The fighting is rooted in a long-standing dispute over land and administrative control between Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regional administrations. Tensions escalated around October 18 over the raising of the Somali regional flag in the disputed Moyale area, reflecting competing claims over territory and authority.

For those arriving in Kenya, the politics are secondary to the immediate question of where they will sleep and what they will feed their children.

Mwasaru Mercy, Kenya’s acting commissioner for refugee affairs, told Al Jazeera that a multi-agency government team had been deployed to Moyale. The Department of Refugee Services is coordinating with local authorities and the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

But gunfire could still be heard, Mercy said, raising fears of further displacement. Many arrivals need food, shelter, bedding and mosquito nets.

“There are no contingency food stocks specifically for this incident because it happened abruptly,” Mercy said.

Authorities are trying to mobilise humanitarian organisations and donors. A refugee camp has not been established because the security situation must improve first. The government is working with UNHCR to register arrivals and assess their needs.
sources.headline: More than 50,000 displaced by deadly Ethiopia border clashes

stories.headline: Trump says FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy

sources.body:
US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.

"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.

Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".

Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology. The revelations knocked about $250bn (£190bn) off its value on Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%.

Trump later told reporters at the White House that the FBI was looking into the issue, but did not elaborate on the investigation, or when it was launched. The FBI declined to comment when contacted by the BBC.

US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang.

According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.

Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Nvidia's Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage.

Megaspeed's office in Singapore's central business district appeared to be operational and staffed on Tuesday.

The BBC was refused entry to its floor, but spoke to a staff member by phone who said they had no comment and directed all queries to the company's PR team.

The BBC has emailed Megaspeed several times for comment.

Nvidia, co-founded by Jensen Huang, is also a major focus in the AI technology race between the US and China, with officials in Washington treating its exports to Beijing as a matter of national security - a key reason why Huang's affair has sparked concerns.

Also on Monday, Huang and Nvidia were sued in a proposed class action lawsuit in California that accuses them of defrauding shareholders by concealing his ties with the suspected Chinese spy.

The lawsuit alleges that the company lied to the media about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, "who is suspected of seeking to help smuggle Nvidia products to China."

The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment on the lawsuit.

At the White House, Trump was asked several times, including by the BBC, when he was made aware of the relationship. He said he was informed "over a period of time" but was not specific.
sources.headline: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sources.body:
US president says he believes CEO Jensen Huang had no knowledge of woman’s alleged work for Chinese intelligence.

United States President Donald Trump has said the FBI is probing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence services.

Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump said law enforcement had begun inquiries following Huang’s admission that he engaged in an extramarital relationship with a Chinese executive named Alice Huang.

“We’ll look into it. I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else,” Trump told reporters at a news conference. “I think he will be in good shape.”

Trump said Huang told him earlier that he had “absolutely no idea” that the woman was an alleged intelligence agent.

“He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump said.

Asked by a reporter when he first became aware of concerns about the relationship, Trump said it was “not too long ago”.

“I have been hearing about it and I have been reading a little bit about it over a period of time,” the US president said.

Nvidia, which dominates the market for high-end chips used to power artificial intelligence, did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Nvidia on Sunday announced that it had opened a probe into its CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, following media reports that cited US intelligence claiming she worked for China’s Ministry of State Security.

Nvidia’s board of directors said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised, but that an independent inquiry overseen by outside counsel would examine “all available information”.

In a separate statement admitting to an extramarital relationship, Huang apologised to his family, colleagues and shareholders, and pledged to cooperate fully with the board’s inquiry.

Huang’s admission came after the New York Times and the Financial Times last week reported that unnamed US officials had authored a memo alleging that he had been targeted by Alice Huang for intelligence-gathering activities.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday rejected the allegations, with spokesperson Guo Jiakun saying the reports were “groundless speculation, and a smear against China”.

Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, has not publicly commented on the claims.

Nvidia, based in Santa Clara, California, is a critical player in the global AI race, controlling an estimated 80 to 90 percent of the market for graphics processing units (GPUs) used to run frontier models.

Shares of Nvidia, one of the world’s most valuable companies, fell 4.27 percent on Monday to close at $178.67.
sources.headline: Trump says FBI probing Nvidia CEO Huang’s affair with alleged spy

stories.headline: Republican Thomas Massie moves to force Hegseth impeachment vote over Iran war

sources.body: Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie moved on Monday to force a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, putting pressure on his fellow Republicans to decide whether to remove one of the Trump administration’s most prominent figures following the party's crushing defeat in midterm elections.
sources.headline: Republican congressman launches impeachment bid against Pentagon chief Hegseth

sources.body:
Outgoing Republican lawmaker Thomas Massie calls on Congress to oust Hegseth over accusations of unlawful orders.

United States Republican Representative Thomas Massie has introduced a resolution to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war on Iran, strikes on purported drug boats and other alleged violations of US laws.

Reading from the text of the resolution in the House of Representatives on Monday, the outgoing Kentucky lawmaker accused Hegseth of carrying out unlawful orders and posing a threat to the Constitution.

Massie introduced the articles of impeachment as soon as the House opened for its first session after the midterm elections. Democratic Party leaders have pledged to investigate US President Donald Trump’s administration in Congress following their landslide victories in both chambers.

Massie reintroduced eight articles of impeachment against the defense secretary that he had first raised in September . Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson avoided a vote in the Republican-led Congress at the time by sending lawmakers home early.

In a news conference on Monday, Massie said he would welcome votes from any lawmakers who want Hegseth removed, even if they have not read the details of his bill.

“I understand that some of them just want to vote for this because they just want to see Hegseth gone,” he said. “I welcome their vote.”

He urged the defense secretary to resign before Democrats take control of Congress in January, predicting their investigations will include testimony from senior administration officials on how the Defense Department has been run under Hegseth.

Hegseth remained defiant, saying he welcomes the opportunity to defend his actions in Congress.

“There’s a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success,” Hegseth told reporters on Monday. “If we want to litigate” the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, he added, “I’m happy to do it all day long.”

He is expected to hold a news conference on Tuesday.

Massie’s resolution alleges that Hegseth violated the Constitution by helping carry out the war on Iran without congressional authorisation, as mandated by the War Powers Resolution.

Hegseth “cultivated a warmaking culture” dismissive of rules of engagement that caused civilian harm, Massie alleges. He cited the US bombing of a school in Minab, Iran, which killed more than 150 people, including about 120 children, at the start of the US-Israel war in February.

The resolution also alleges that US strikes on alleged narcotics boats in the Caribbean and Pacific ignored mandatory safeguards and amounted to extrajudicial killings by Hegseth.

Other charges against Hegseth involve the abduction of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, suppressing free speech by restricting media access to the Pentagon and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen against the Houthis.

Massie has been a frequent critic of Trump’s administration, particularly the Iran war. His outspoken nature has previously drawn anger from Trump, who backed a rival Republican candidate who defeated Massie in the primary elections earlier this year.
sources.headline: US congressman files resolution to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth

sources.body:
A Republican congressman plans to force a vote in the House of Representatives this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he has violated the US Constitution.

"By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Representative Thomas Massie said.

The effort will likely fail, as Republicans remain in power in Congress until January. But Massie says the effort is aimed at pushing President Donald Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.

Hegseth has called the impeachment effort a "sham" and defended his record.

"You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective," he said in a video statement last week. "It's not going to work. We will not back down."

He called Massie a "disgruntled, defeated congressman" and said he was not concerned about the impeachment effort. In the video, Hegseth defended his leadership of the department and listed ways he has fulfilled Trump's America First agenda.

Massie formally introduced his articles of impeachment in a resolution on the House floor on Monday afternoon. The move starts a 48-hour clock for the chamber to take up the measure. Lawmakers could vote on the resolution directly, vote to refer it to committee or to set it aside.

"I'm doing this because it's the right thing to do," he told reporters after introducing the articles.

Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it started nearly nine months ago. He has previously garnered headlines over demanding the Trump administration release the files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The Kentucky congressman first introduced impeachment articles in September and has now brought them back in the wake of Republicans losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections.

He has said the effort was aimed at preventing a Democrat spectacle next year when they have control of Congress. He said he hoped to force Trump to name a replacement, who could be quickly confirmed while Republicans have power.

"My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie also said in a statement. "They will hold hearings and trials."

Democratic leadership has signalled openness to such an effort against Hegseth once they take control in January.

Asked about the effort on Monday, Hegseth said, "We're not worried about that".

He said he planned to hold a news conference on Tuesday to discuss the subject.

President Trump has indicated that he plans to stick by Hegseth , praising his leadership in the US capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro earlier this year and defending his work during the war in Iran.

"We've made the world a lot safer place. Why haven't we gone after all these other people that ran wars and lost?" Trump said on Monday at the White House.
sources.headline: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth

stories.headline: Trump reverses stance and alleges fraud in the midterm elections

sources.body:
Democratic Senate leader Schumer criticises Trump’s poll denialism, calling it an avoidable return to baseless claims.

United States President Donald Trump has questioned the integrity of last week’s midterm elections, reversing course less than a week after congratulating Democrats on their victories and saying he was willing to accept the results.

“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post on Monday. “How could the Polls be so wrong???”

While Republicans questioned whether polls were once again underestimating their support, as they had in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 presidential elections, the results ultimately went the other way.

Polls had largely pointed to a strong night for Democrats, with surveys suggesting the party was well positioned to take control of the House of Representatives and had a realistic chance of winning the Senate.

In fact, Pew Research released a report analysing pre-election polling data and found that the data understated the Democratic margin by at least 2 points in 23 of 27 races for governor and the US Senate.

Trump also alleged on Truth Social that some early voting ballot counts were so large that they made it impossible for Republicans to win. He provided no evidence of election fraud or wrongdoing. Over the past few days, the president has shared posts on Truth Social with graphs questioning voter turnout data.

The post marks Trump’s first explicit public challenge to the integrity of the overall midterm results since Democrats overwhelmingly won control of both chambers of Congress, in addition to a string of victories in traditionally Republican strongholds.

This latest remark comes a day after an interview with CBS’s 60 Minutes, in which Trump appeared to accept the election outcome. Asked about his decision to congratulate Democrats, Trump confirmed that he had done so and said he was open to working with the incoming Democratic majority.

Shortly after the Democratic Party’s victory was announced, Trump congratulated them on a call with CBS News and later told Fox News that the party “did a good job”.

He had also told The New York Times last week that he “absolutely” accepted the results of the election.

Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer responded to Trump’s latest remarks, saying the president’s “return to election denialism was inevitable”.

“He can whine all he wants, but nothing will stop this inescapable truth: For the last two years of his presidency, Trump will face the largest Democratic congressional majorities in decades, all because he has been an unprecedented failure,” Schumer wrote on X.

Republicans have increasingly sought to distance themselves from Trump following the party’s midterm losses. Even conservative commentator Megyn Kelly, who supported the president in 2024, responded on X to his election fraud claims with a blunt “Just stop.”

El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, en su llegada a la Cas Blanca este domingo.

La derrota de los republicanos en las elecciones legislativas de medio mandato fue tan aplastante que Donald Trump no tuvo otra opción que abandonar su discurso del fraude electoral, que llevaba todo el año alimentando y, en el fondo, desde que dio el salto a la política hace una década. En la misma noche electoral, el martes pasado, Trump reconoció la derrota, aceptó los resultados y expresó disposición a negociar con las nuevas mayorías demócratas en el Congreso. Pero no se ha podido contener más: este lunes ha publicado en su plataforma, Truth Social, un mensaje que pone en duda la limpieza de los comicios.

“¿De verdad hay alguien que crea que estas 'elecciones' fueron honestas? ¿Cómo es posible que las encuestas se equivocaran tanto? Algunos de los primeros 'aluviones' de votos anticipados fueron tan grandes que resultaba imposible ganar, por muchas personas que acudieran a votar. Todo gira en torno a las máquinas de votación, ¡que son mucho más importantes que los votantes!”, ha dicho el presidente.

No hay ninguna prueba o sospecha creíble, ni ninguna sentencia judicial que acredite la existencia de fraude electoral en favor del Partido Demócrata. Tampoco los había en el 2020, pero Trump siguió impulsando esa mentira hasta las últimas consecuencias, en un episodio oscuro que llevó a sus seguidores a asaltar el Capitolio el 6 de enero del 2021, en el mayor ataque a la democracia estadounidense desde la guerra civil.

En este ciclo electoral, el presidente ha tratado de interferir de forma muy evidente en la organización de los comicios, que según la Constitución es competencia de los estados. Entre otras actuaciones, despidió a los encargados federales de supervisar y dar consejo a los estados en los comicios y creó un plan para tomar el control sobre el reparto de papeletas tan solo a personas autorizadas por el Gobierno.

El Departamento de Justicia llegó a denunciar al estado de California para intentar que se detuviera el recuento de 20.000 votos de personas que, según su departamento de Seguridad Nacional, “probablemente” no eran ciudadanas. El Tribunal Supremo terminó rechazando este recurso, después de que tribunales inferiores hicieran lo propio, alegando que era inconstitucional y que no había pruebas de que aquellas personas no tuvieran derecho a voto.

La Administración Trump también denunció a Alaska y está tratando de invalidar el resultado de sus comicios al Senado en caso de que el candidato republicano, Dan Sullivan, pierda las elecciones. El motivo es que hay un tercer candidato con el mismo nombre que, según una exclusiva de The New York Times, fue reclutado por la candidata demócrata Mary Peltola.

Aunque no ha tomado medidas concretas contra las máquinas de recuento, ese fue uno de los argumentos centrales de la teoría del fraude electoral en el 2020. La idea, que compraron muchos seguidores del movimiento MAGA, era que la empresa Dominion Voting Machines, una de las encargadas del recuento en varios estados, manipuló los votos recibidos para dar la victoria a Joe Biden.

sources.body:
El Gobierno plantea paralizar TikTok en España por denuncias de abuso sexual infantil. En la foto, una niña, en una acción de denuncia contra los abusos sexuales infantiles. / MAURICIO OSORIO / EFE / VÍDEO: EUROPA PRESS

La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego , ha anunciado este lunes que su ministerio ha solicitado a la Fiscalía General del Estado que abra una investigación contra TikTok por permitir en su plataforma miles de vídeos de abuso sexual infantil y la comunicación entre pederastas. A la vez, ha abierto la puerta a paralizar la plataform a ante "la falta de mecanismos eficaces en la red social para impedir la difusión de dicho material ".

La decisión de la ministra ha sido provocada por una investigación de Maldita.es, que ha detectado en TikTok más de mil vídeos de abuso sexual infantil , con 48 millones de visualizaciones , y más de 20.000 perfiles de potenciales pedófilos que intercambian o venden este tipo de material, de los que más de 7.000 operan en castellano . Titulada 'El hogar pederasta en TikTok', la investigación también ha localizado 780 cuentas que utilizan la plataforma para captar a compradores de material de abuso sexual infantil , 91 emisiones en directo de menores en 17 países en los que los usuarios piden acciones, a veces sexuales, a cambio de dinero, y una comunidad de más de 2.000 miembros que busca contenido de bebés.

En el escrito trasladado a la Fiscalía, el ministerio incluye la información conocida para que, en el ejercicio de sus competencias, adopte las medidas necesarias para garantizar la protección integral de los niños, niñas y adolescentes que puedan estar afectados. Además, tras plantear la posibilidad de paralizar los servicios de la plataforma en España , si así se considerase oportuno, la ministra Rego ha pedido a los representantes de la plataforma en España una reunión con carácter urgente para conocer las explicaciones de TikTok, así como las medidas adoptadas y las actuaciones inmediatas previstas para garantizar la protección de la infancia y la adolescencia en su plataforma.

No es la primera vez que el Gobierno pide endurecer la regulación de las plataformas digitales. En febrero, el Consejo de Ministros reclamó al Ministerio Fiscal que investigara "los delitos que X, Meta y TikTok podrían estar cometiendo por la creación y difusión de pornografía infantil mediante sus IA" . "Estas plataformas están atentando contra la salud mental, la dignidad y los derechos de nuestros hijos e hijas. El Estado no lo puede permitir. La impunidad de los gigantes debe acabar", justificó el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, a través de un mensaje publicado precisamente en la red social propiedad de Elon Musk. El proyecto de ley de protección digital en la infancia y adolescencia –que nació con el objetivo de prohibir el acceso a redes sociales a menores de 16 años– se ha quedado en un cajón debido al parón parlamentario por la convocatoria electoral.

Los procedimientos judiciales incoados por delitos relacionados con la pornografía infantil a través de las nuevas tecnologías aumentaron un 26,3% en España durante 2025, hasta alcanzar los 865 casos, frente a los 685 registrados el año anterior. Según la 'Memoria 2026' de la Fiscalía General del Estado, el incremento se sitúa en torno al 41% respecto a 2023. Los fiscales advierten de la gravedad de las conductas investigadas y de la creciente elaboración de material de abuso sexual infantil.
sources.headline: El Gobierno se plantea paralizar TikTok en España tras detectarse más de mil vídeos de abuso sexual infantil

sources.body:
La plataforma maldita.es ha publicado la primera entrega de una investigación propia titulada TikTok, el hogar del pederasta en la que señala haber encontrado con las herramientas de búsqueda abiertas a todo el mundo 1.182 contenidos de abuso sexual infantil explícito en TikTok, aportados por unos 200 perfiles, que cuentan con 48 millones de visualizaciones de vídeos que muestran ese tipo de material explícito. Ante estas informaciones, el Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia ha remitido un escrito a la Fiscalía General del Estado para que actúe, por considerarlo de “extrema gravedad” y se plantea incluso la suspensión de la red social. TikTok, por su parte, reclama conocer la investigación al completo para poder actuar.

La investigación de maldita.es se llevó a cabo entre el 11 de septiembre y el 15 de octubre de este año. Según este medio, TikTok ha eliminado una parte de esos vídeos encontrados, aunque “muchos siguen disponibles”. La política de la plataforma de vídeo sobre este tipo de abusos contempla la prohibición de las cuentas que los publican, aunque según la investigación, a 15 de octubre, 136 de las 231 cuentas que habían analizado, el 59% seguían todavía activas.

El informe asegura que de entre esos más de mil vídeos hallados, maldita.es ha denunciado una muestra de 50 a TikTok a través de su sistema de moderación, aunque sólo ha sido borrado el 10%. “A fecha de publicación de este artículo y después de haber contactado a TikTok, la plataforma se ha limitado a pedir más información, pero no ha respondido a nuestras consultas sobre sus mecanismos de protección de menores, los fallos detectados y los hallazgos de contenido ilegal en su plataforma”, asegura el medio en su página web.

Maldita afirma “muchos de los perfiles detectados funcionan como auténticos catálogos de material de abuso sexual infantil”. Se refiere a publicaciones que “muestran fotografías de las víctimas sobre las que superponen, mediante transparencias, fotogramas de los vídeos de abuso que ofrecen, indicando en ocasiones su precio o duración”. Según la plataforma periodística, se trata de “cuentas dedicadas casi exclusivamente a esta actividad ilegal que permanecen activas en TikTok, acumulando visualizaciones, seguidores y ‘me gusta’ sin que los sistemas de moderación de la plataforma las retiren”.

En el informe se pregunta si quienes se dedican a vender material de abuso sexual infantil son “especialmente hábiles a la hora de esquivar los controles de TikTok o es que los mecanismos de moderación de la plataforma no funcionan”. No hay una respuesta, aunque se apunta que si la red social conoce la existencia de esas técnicas, “no está actuando de forma eficaz para eliminarlas de manera sistemática”. Los investigadores señalan que el algoritmo de selección de TikTok, “poco a poco, acaba conduciendo a los usuarios hasta estos contenidos”.

La investigación muestra algunas de las técnicas de los perfiles que publican el material de abusos, con texto superpuesto sobre imágenes, o algunas fotografías pixeladas que conducen a otros canales, como Telegram y Zangi, en el que se ofrecen los fotogramas completos de las imágenes de los menores abusados sexualmente y se invita a comprar ese contenido.
sources.headline: El Gobierno se plantea cerrar TikTok en España por permitir abuso sexual infantil

El govern espanyol ha demanat a la Fiscalia que actuï i contempli la possibilitat de tancar TikTok a Espanya , després d'una investigació de Maldita.es que ha destapat una allau de material pedòfil a la plataforma.

El Ministeri de Joventut i Infància ha enviat un escrit a la Fiscalia, on insta a investigar els presumptes casos d'abús sexual infantil i denuncia "la manca de mecanismes eficaços a la xarxa social per impedir la difusió d'aquest contingut".

Sobre aquesta qüestió, el president espanyol, Pedro Sánchez, ha dit que no descarta "suspendre" TikTok : "Em sembla un escàndol i cal investigar-ho, saber exactament quin perímetre penal té aquesta notícia". Ho ha dit en una entrevista a La Séptima, on també ha afegit que s'actuarà "amb l'absoluta contundència i proporcionalment a la gravetat d'aquest assumpte".

A més, la ministra de Joventut i Infància, Sira Rego, també ha informat la decisió de demanar una reunió "urgent" amb la plataforma per tal d'aclarir la situació: "La investigació mostra que no s'estarien prenent les mesures i salvaguardes establertes per la Unió Europea. Creiem que TikTok ha de donar una explicació clara sobre el que està passant", ha apuntat Rego.

La recerca de Maldita.es , un mitjà dedicat al periodisme de verificació, ha detectat més de mil vídeos d'abús sexual infantil a TikTok, amb més de 48 milions de visualitzacions, i 26.000 perfils que intercanvien o venen aquest material.

També han trobat 780 comptes dedicats a captar compradors de fotos i vídeos d'abús infantil i una comunitat de més de 2.000 membres que busca contingut de bebès.

A més, s'han localitzat 91 emissions en directe de menors en 17 països, en les quals els usuaris demanen que facin accions, sovint sexuals, a canvi de diners.

És la tercera investigació de Maldita.es per denunciar la inacció de TikTok davant el contingut d'explotació sexual infantil. Denuncien que el buscador de la plataforma és "una eina sense filtres per a un pedòfil".

Els investigadors asseguren que, gràcies a l'algoritme, poden trobar aquest tipus de contingut. De fet, expliquen que ells mateixos van trobar una violació en directe d'un bebè.

Durant 35 dies els especialistes han analitzat perfils, comentaris i emissions en directe i han creat comptes per investigar com es comporta l'algoritme.

Han documentat activitat principalment a Espanya, Tailàndia, el Vietnam, Myanmar i Rússia , i també a altres països de la Unió Europea i l'Amèrica Llatina.

Alguns dels usuaris han reconegut a Maldita.es que tenen material dels seus fills o nebots. Segons els investigadors, molts dels vídeos es graven en domicilis o en escoles , amb menors que retransmeten en directe des de les aules, els lavabos o durant l'hora del pati.

Segons Maldita.es, TikTok no posa traves perquè s'emetin i es publiquin aquests continguts, sinó que els "publicita" i "hi guanya diners".

Arran de la investigació, han denunciat una cinquantena de vídeos amb material explícit, que acumulen 8,9 milions de visualitzacions i més de 150.000 "m'agrada". D'aquests, asseguren que la plataforma n'ha retirat cinc i n'ha bloquejat 13 només a Espanya. Tres dies després de la denúncia, el 40% dels comptes continuaven actius.

Control policial en los accesos al Port de Tarragona durante la huelga del metal, que ha bloqueado la entrada y salida de mercancías este lunes. / PORT DE TARRAGONA / Europa Press

Los Mossos d'Esquadra ultima preparativos para la huelga general de este 11 de noviembre, una jornada que califican de "atípica" y en la que esperan "disturbios". La policía espera horas "complicadas" y por ello ha decretado un nivel 4 de riesgo, que es el máximo, dado que esperan la presencia de "grupos combativos" que coincidirán "con un gran volumen de personas manifestándose".

Es por ello que se ha diseñado un dispositivo de máximos. El despliegue policial será de unos 9.000 agentes; un 50% más de los que suelen trabajar en un día normal; o lo que es lo mismo; 3.000 más. Estarán repartidos en cuatro turnos: el primero empezará la víspera, el día 10 de noviembre a las 22.00 horas. Le seguirán el turno de mañana, tarde y noche del día 11 y el operativo concluirá a las 00.00 del 12 de noviembre. Del total de 9.000 agentes, 1.400 estarán destinados en Barcelona.

Los agentes centrarán buena parte de su atención en la movilidad de las grandes arterias, como la AP-7, la A-2, la C-17, la B-23, la C-58 y los principales accesos a Barcelona. Se estima que a las 6 o 7 de la mañana del miércoles ya habrá afectaciones "graves" e importantes colapsos en la movilidad en toda Catalunya, y se prevén incidencias en centros logísticos, polígonos industriales, puertos y aeropuertos. Los Mossos insisten en pedir a la ciudadanía que se informe antes de desplazarse y que, en cualquier caso, lo haga con mucho margen de tiempo.

La actividad policial, explican, estará centrada en "evitar bloqueos" y restablecer la movilidad afectada. En este sentido, los Mossos buscarán "el equilibrio" entre garantizar el derecho a la huelga y garantizar el derecho a la libre circulación de quienes quieran desplazarse o acudir a trabajar. Habrá mediación y se actuará ante cada corte de manera "quirúrgica", en función de la vía afectada, el riesgo para las personas o la repercusión sobre los servicios de emergencia, entre otros factores.

Hay numerosas concentraciones y manifestaciones comunicadas por todo el territorio, aunque la que se espera que sea más multitudinaria es la del miércoles por la tarde en los Jardinets de Gràcia de Barcelona, convocada a las 17.30 horas . Se ha calificado con un nivel de riesgo 4, el máximo posible, porque, al poder superar las 50.000 personas , los Mossos consideran probable que también atraiga a "grupos combativos".

En este sentido, preocupa que puedan producirse disturbios, barricadas, incendios o agresiones a policías, además de la presencia de grupos que aprovechen la situación para cometer saqueos. "Es probable que haya disturbios y que la manifestación de la tarde acabe con destrozos y que determinadas personas intenten sabotear comercios o persigan otros objetivos desestabilizadores", admiten. En caso de disturbios no se descarta el uso de gas pimienta si se considera necesario.
sources.headline: Los Mossos activan la alerta máxima el 11-N y movilizan a 9.000 agentes; un 50% más que un día normal

sources.body:
Dues preocupacions té ara com ara la Prefectura dels Mossos d’Esquadra de cara la vaga general convocada el dimecres 11 de novembre. En concret, la mobilitat i la manifestació prevista a quarts de sis de la tarda al capdamunt del passeig de Gràcia de Barcelona. Dos neguits que han suposat una preparació extraordinària de recursos i més en un context global de protestes violentes i amb aldarulls arreu d’Europa com ha passat a França, Itàlia o Albània i el reflux de les protestes “extraordinàries” del 24 d’octubre a Barcelona arran de la convocatòria de Blocus. Tot i que des de Mossos asseguren que no preveuen que aquest moviment actuï durant la vaga general.

Així, la Prefectura mobilitzarà 9.000 mossos, és a dir, un 50% més dels que estan en servei en un dia feiner. Un servei de 32 hores dividits en quatre torns per prevenir i actuar en els efectes de la vaga i, sobretot, no deixar coix el servei ordinari. Un dispositiu que implica el reforç de les plantilles ordinàries d’unitats d’ordre públic -Brigada Mòbil o Àrees Regionals de Recursos Operatius (ARRO)-, seguretat ciutadana, mediació, trànsit, o xarxes que patrullarà per la xarxa i estarà amatent a qualsevol fet que assenyali una estratègia híbrida, és a dir, de batussa al carrer combinada amb efectes digitals d’internet.

La intenció és controlar la mobilitat i garantir la dualitat de drets, entre els vaguistes i els que no volen secundar la vaga, i sobretot, evitar que la manifestació de la tarda, on és previst que se superin en escreix la xifra dels cinquanta mil assistents, sigui una batalla campal. De fet, els Mossos avaluen -seguint els criteris de les prospectives de la Comissaria General d’Informació- la manifestació de la tarda de nivell 4 sobre 4 , és a dir, amb “episodis combatius, com ara crema de contenidors, atacs vandàlics o enfrontaments amb la policia”. En tot cas, Mossos recorda que a la “caixa d’eines” hi tenen molts elements com l’esprai pebre, la defensa, el casc, les manilles, els gasos lacrimògens o pots de fum, malgrat que les dues darreres opcions fa més de 15 anys que no s’utilitzen. Com el conjunt de les policies europees.

Els informes i l’històric amb què treballava la policia de la Generalitat els fan concloure que no es troben davant una convocatòria habitual. De fet, raonen que els objectius són “més socials que no pas laborals” i, per tant, més difusos. És a dir, arran de l’habitatge s’hi han afegit més demandes que despisten el que poden ser els objectius habituals de les protestes com ara la Borsa de Barcelona, Foment del Treball, la delegació del govern espanyol a Catalunya. L’amalgama de motius pels quals els convoca la vaga fa que Mossos no pugui establir quins escenaris poden ser els més proclius a ser objecte d’actes de protesta o d’aldarulls i també poder bloquejar intents de pillatge o saqueig. A més, tenen present que també hi ha convocades vagues de maquinistes de Renfe i del sector carni que avui ja han afectat a punts de la Garrotxa i Osona.

stories.headline: Barcelona Airbnb listings fall 20% in a year to their lowest level since 2015

sources.body: L’ oferta de pisos turístics a Airbnb continua a la baixa a Barcelona. Segons ha avançat RAC1, el nombre d’anuncis actius a la plataforma ha disminuït un 20 % en només un any i se situa en poc més de 15.200. Això representa més de 4.000 anuncis menys que fa 12 mesos i suposa la xifra més baixa des del 2015 , quan Airbnb va començar a créixer amb força a la capital catalana. Les dades, facilitades per l’Ajuntament, també indiquen que d’aquest 20 %, sis de cada 10 dels pisos anunciats són il·legals . També et pot interessar El final dels pisos turístics: com afectarà el mercat laboral i el PIB de Barcelona? Helena Molist Sancho Olga Borràs Boada 3 minuts de lectura 300 anuncis il·legals cada mes La primera tinenta d’alcaldia, Laia Bonet , ha valorat positivament aquestes xifres en una atenció als mitjans aquest dilluns. Bonet atribueix la reducció dels anuncis a la feina d’inspecció i control que fa l’Ajuntament, que cada mes comunica a Airbnb els pisos turístics que no compleixen la normativa perquè la plataforma els retiri. Segons ha explicat, actualment el consistori trasllada al voltant de 300 anuncis il·legals cada mes . Tot i aquesta reducció, Bonet considera que encara cal avançar més i ha reclamat a Airbnb que actuï de manera preventiva per evitar que es publiquin anuncis que no compleixen els requisits legals. Aquesta és una de les mesures que l’Ajuntament vol incloure en un conveni amb la plataforma, però que encara no s’ha signat. A més, la tinenta d’alcaldia ha recordat que el consistori també treballa per recuperar habitatges que tenien llicència turística , però que no han començat a funcionar com a allotjaments durant els primers tres mesos. En aquests casos, l’Ajuntament pot retirar-ne la llicència, com ja ha fet amb un pis del carrer de Tarragona. També et pot interessar Un tallat surt més car als barris amb més pisos turístics anunciats a Airbnb Clara Aliaguilla 2 minuts de lectura

stories.headline: Muntaner enters quieter phase of L8 construction as heavy drilling equipment is dismantled

sources.body: La part més sorollosa de les obres del perllongament de l’L8 al carrer de Muntaner està a punt d’arribar a la seva fi. Han acabat de perforar el pou de la sortida d’emergència per col·locar-hi les pantalles de contenció i, ara, ja comencen a desmuntar l’enorme maquinària que ha envaït el carrer durant mesos. Després seguiran les obres per excavar el pou amb excavadores més petites , però, segons els tècnics, ja no causarà tantes molèsties. La previsió és que a principis de l’any que ve es pugui reobrir el trànsit al carrer de Muntaner amb dos carrils de circulació, tot i que s’haurà de tornar a tallar més endavant. Els veïns n’estan fins al monyo El soroll al carrer de Muntaner durant els últims quatre mesos ha estat intens. “Realment és insuportable : el soroll, la pols, aquest remenament, el carrer tallat, l’accés al pàrquing, tot és un desastre, vull dir que ja n’estem fins aquí dalt, ja no podem més “, explica Assumpció Lleonsi, que ve tres vegades a la setmana al carrer de Muntaner a visitar la seva filla. La Marta Brossa, una altra veïna, també n’ha tingut prou: “La veritat és que ho porto malament perquè no sabem quan acabarà , hi ha molt soroll, cada matí passo per aquí i fa respecte. I pel comerç també ha anat molt malament, es nota que la gent no passa tant”, explica. Les obres han tingut un gran impacte acústic i visual al carrer Cau la venda, puja el soroll Les obres han tingut un fort impacte en els comerços de la zona. Laia Bueno, de la sabateria Casas, explica que dissabte a la tarda només va vendre un parell de sabates i que amb prou feines van entrar cinc persones a la botiga. Assegura que abans era un carrer amb moviment, però que les restriccions derivades de les obres, sense cotxes ni autobusos, han fet caure molt el pas de vianants i, de retruc, les vendes . La situació també ha afectat de ple un bufet d’advocats situat just al costat de la perforadora. El soroll ha estat tan intens que han hagut de deixar d’utilitzar les sales de reunions que donen al carrer de Muntaner i traslladar les trobades als espais interiors. “ Treballar en aquestes condicions és molt molest . Tenir una reunió de dues hores en una sala interior no és el mateix que fer-la a les exteriors. Fins i tot, per evitar molèsties, alguns companys han optat pel teletreball “, explica Antonio Sala, de Tornos Abogados. Una part important de l’obra, acabada L’execució de les pantalles del pou de la sortida d’emergència de l’L8 al carrer de Muntaner va acabar el dissabte 31 d’octubre. Això ha permès començar a desmuntar la hidrofressa (perforadora) i les sitges on s’abocava la terra que s’extreia durant les perforacions. La previsió és que d’aquí a tres setmanes s’hagin retirat tant la màquina com les instal·lacions auxiliars i llavors els treballs al pou continuaran amb excavadores més petites i, per tant, amb menys soroll . Pel que fa al tancament acústic , s’anirà retirant progressivament . Veïns i comerciants esperen que aquest canvi marqui un punt d’inflexió després de mesos de molèsties. “Si ja treuen aquest trasto enorme doncs anem avançant… l’important és que avancin”, conclou Brossa. La perforadora i les sitges hauran desaparegut del carrer a finals de novembre Les obres dels últims quatre mesos han servit per fer les parets de contenció del pou de la sortida d’emergència de l’L8. El pou té nou metres de diàmetre i 62 de profunditat . Les pantalles, però, arriben fins als 86 metres. Tot i els avanços, encara falta molt perquè la tuneladora arribi a Muntaner i es connecti amb el pou. També et pot interessar L’agonia dels comerços de Muntaner afectats per les obres de l’L8: “N’hi ha molts que volen tancar” Montse Llorens 2 minuts de lectura

stories.headline: Barcelona visitor numbers rise 4.7% through September as tourism growth slows

sources.body:
Ambiente de turistas asiáticos alrededor de la Sagrada Família, el 9 de noviembre de 2026. / MANU MITRU

El turismo, en Barcelona, crece en el acumulado del año impulsado por los meses de verano, pero también por el sólido dinamismo de un mes de septiembre. El número de visitantes acumulado durante los nueve primeros meses de 2026 ha superado los 7,1 millones de personas, un 4,7% más que en el mismo periodo del último año. Los últimos datos con los que trabaja el Ayuntamiento de Barcelona apuntan a un comportamiento notable del sector en el noveno mes del año, con un aumento del 5% del número de turistas alojados en los hoteles de la ciudad, hasta alcanzar las 830.000 personas.

El sector avanza, eso sí, con algunas particularidades. La tendencia apunta hacia una clara consolidación del visitante extracomunitario como el principal y un acercamiento al porcentaje de turistas nacionales, que se estancan, al menos en septiembre. Los turistas estadounidenses que visitan la ciudad están solamente un 9,8% por debajo del total de visitantes nacionales. En la misma línea, los asiáticos, y más concretamente los turistas chinos, crecen al ritmo del 33%.

En ambos casos, tanto para el turista de fuera de la Unión como para el doméstico , la media de estancias por persona se estanca e incluso se reduce ligeramente con respecto al mismo mes del año pasado. La media de estancias se sitúa en 2,32 por persona, mientras fue de 2,37 en septiembre de 2025. Mayor número de turistas, por lo tanto, pero que se quedan en la ciudad para estancias más cortas. En septiembre, las pernoctaciones superaron los 1,9 millones, un 2,5% más interanual. El aumento se situó en el 2,7% en el caso de los turistas de nacionalidad extranjera.

A lo largo del año, los turistas llegados de países de fuera de la Unión Europea que se han alojado en hoteles de la ciudad han representado casi el 53% del total, equivalente a 3,8 millones de viajeros. Frente a este porcentaje destaca el del turismo nacional, que copa el 16,7% del total. Los visitantes procedentes de países de la Unión Europea han ascendido al 30,3% del total.

En este contexto, toman especial relevancia los viajeros estadounidenses, que suelen elegir Barcelona como una de sus principales destinaciones en verano . En el acumulado hasta septiembre, Barcelona recibió cerca de 1,2 millones de turistas estadounidenses, solo un 9,8% menos de visitantes que el cómputo global de turistas nacionales. El porcentaje de turistas llegados de Estados Unidos creció un 11,8% en el periodo analizado. Sin embargo, en el noveno mes del año, el turismo estadounidense ya superó la media del nacional, siendo el 17,8% del total.

Por detrás de los estadounidenses se sitúan los españoles, copando el 14,9% del total de turistas alojados en hoteles en septiembre. En tercer lugar, se sitúan los turistas de Reino Unido, que conforman el 7,6% del total y, en cuarta posición, los alemanes, con el 5,1%. El quinto puesto es para los turistas franceses (son el 4,4%), seguidos de cerca por Francia, con el 4,2%. Los chinos, en septiembre, se han situado como la séptima nacionalidad que más visita Barcelona. El 85% de las personas que llegan a la ciudad en septiembre tienen perfil internacional.
sources.headline: El turismo crece en Barcelona: 4,7% más de visitantes hasta septiembre, con estadounidenses y chinos al frente

sources.body:
Turistas en el paseo de Gràcia, el pasado septiembre. / Jordi Otix / EPC

Tras nueve meses en los que Barcelona ha incrementado su volumen de turistas alojados en hoteles, como informa hoy este diario, las previsiones de la recta final de año apuntan a la estabilidad o ligero descenso . El Observatorio del Turismo en Barcelona, en su último análisis de perspectivas para la capital catalana apunta a un volumen de reservas inferior al año pasado este noviembre y algo superior en diciembre . No obstante, son datos provisionales que dependerán de las peticiones de última hora que se deciden en función de variables que van de la meteorología a las ofertas de precios.

El informe apunta también que las reservas registradas hasta ahora se han hecho con más anticipación que en 2025, una media de 53 días. Frente a la moderación del presente mes, el mes de diciembre tiene mejores previones que un año antes. La estancia promedio prevista es de 3,1 noches.

Respecto a la tendencia en los perfiles de los visitantes, los datos de octubre ya consolidados muestran que un 31,6% de las reservas finales fueron del resto del España, seguidas por un 12,3% de EEUU; un 6,7% de Reino Unido, y un 6,1% de Francia. La mitad (54,3%) eran de viajes en pareja, seguidas por visitantes en solitario (27,1%) y en grupo (12.9%). El volumen de familias es residual en otoño e invierno, salvo periodos vacacionales.

Para el próximo trimestre , en la previsión realizada por el observatorio con datos de The Hotels Network, respecto a otros destinos competidores analizados Barcelona es quinta en volumen de reservas . Madrid está a la cabeza (también en el listado del pasado trimestre), seguida por Viena, Amsterdam, Londres y Berlín.

En lo referente a precios , Londres está a la cabeza a una tarifa media diaria de 398 euros entre noviembre y enero próximo, seguida por París (271), Madrid (263) y otras. Barcelona se queda en 224 euros , por delante de Berlín en este listado.

El turismo profesional toma el relevo al vacacional en otoño, aunque noviembre no será un mes especialmente destacado. La capital catalana tiene confirmados 42 congresos en noviembre, aunque la mayoría de pequeño formato. El de más peso, con más de 25.000 asistentes, el Smart City Expo World Congress ya tuvo lugar la semana pasada. Mientras que el segundo más destacado, el IBTM World se celebrará la próxima y aglutinará unos 13.000 participantes. El total mensual será de algo más de 50.000 congresistas. La actividad cae a mínimos en diciembre, por las fiestas navideñas.

En cuanto a capacidad aérea, aunque afecta tanto a la llegada de turistas, como a los desplazamientos de los catalanes, en noviembre el aeropuerto barcelonés ofrecerá vuelos con un total 5,1 millones de asientos, y en diciembre 5,4, lo que supone un aumento del 3,8 y 4,6%, respectivamente. Serán un total de 192 rutas (+4,3) de las que 64 son intercontinentales (+25,5%), aunque en este periodo descienden ligeramente hasta 82 las compañías aéreas operativas.

El sector de los cruceros sumará 74 salidas y escalas de buques, algo por debajo de 2025, aunque el volumen de cruceristas dependerá de su ocupación final.
sources.headline: El auge del turismo en Barcelona frena y se mantendrá estable en la recta final de 2026
